{{Quote|To be honest, I don't really like the way the Empire seems to treat their pilots. They seem too much like fodder to me.|[[Prost Roberts]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:PRaup">{{SWGcite|exp=JtL|type=conversation|Prost Roberts (an untrained pilot)|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
The ''' Starfighter Corps''',<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-10-the-rise-of-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 10: The Rise of the Empire}} {{1stID|Starfighter Corps}}</ref> also known simply as '''Imperial pilot corp''',<ref name="Owner's Technical Manual">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref> was a component of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] under the aegis of [[Flight Branch]] that controlled the Navy's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]].

==History==
===Origins===
[[File:Black_Squadron_Assault_TCB_by_Nash.jpg|thumb|left|200px|TIE Fighters of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Black Squadron (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Black Squadron]] launching at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].]]
After the [[Declaration of a New Order]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Republic Starfighter Corps/Legends|Republic Starfighter Corps]] lost its status as an independent arm of the military and was merged with the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. Unlike the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], the Imperial Navy's doctrine focused on [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] firepower rather than starfighter superiority and it subordinated the Starfighter Corps to this role.<ref name="Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> Consequently, the Empire turned away from [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighter]] development, seeing it as a distasteful legacy of the great swarms of [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Vulture droid starfighters]] deployed by the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The Empire instead focused on the creation of a new generation of space superiority fighters, culminating in [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]' [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] of starfighters.

The [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN Line Starfighter]] and the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/SA Bomber]] were barebones fighter designs built around a ball-shaped cockpit and [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar's]] revolutionary [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engine]] design. Seen as complements to [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], they served as escorts, scouts, hit-and-fade raiders, and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] supporting ground troops. As such, they lacked [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]], [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], or even life support systems, reducing their mass and giving them great speed and maneuverability, but also limiting their survivability and their range.<ref name="Warfare" />

TIE Fighters were deployed from the [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Strikefast/Legends|''Strikefast'']] as early as one week after the Declaration of a New Order, and they generally served the Starfighter Corps well during the [[Reconquest of the Rim]] and the campaigns against the last [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]] during the early [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], piloted by such Imperial [[Ace/Legends|aces]] as [[Shea Hublin]]. The Corps' doctrine went largely unchallenged until the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] emerged as a credible opponent to the Empire after [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="Warfare" /> In time, the TIE Fighter came to be the most potent symbol of the Imperial Navy's control of space.<ref name="Vehicles">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>

===The Galactic Civil War===
[[File:Pincer5.jpg|thumb|right|200px|TIE Interceptors in the attack at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].]]
The [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps's]] doctrine during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] was built around shielded, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable starfighters that were capable of long-range independent operations, were fast enough to counter TIE Fighters, and carried payloads powerful enough to bring down the shields of large [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]]. The Empire suffered an outright humiliation at the [[Fei Hu campaign]] in 1 BBY, where the Rebel [[Lightspeed Panthers]], equipped with the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]], destroyed 265 Imperial fighters over the course of nine months with the loss of only four of their own.<ref name="Warfare" />

The subsequent Imperial defeat at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and the destruction of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|First Death Star]] led the Starfighter Corps to begin mass production of the much faster, much more maneuverable [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]], and to investigate development of its own [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]]. However, both sheer cost and institutional opposition within the Navy meant that the [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE/AD "Avenger"]] and the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]] would never see action outside of limited deployments.<ref name="Warfare" /> The Starfighter Corps attempted to redeem the humiliating defeat at Yavin with the victory at the [[Second Battle of Ord Biniir]], which so happened to have occurred on the same day. The [[2/181st|second squadron]] of the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Wing]] under the command of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] successfully engaged and destroyed numerous Rebel [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing starfighters]] and recaptured [[Ord Biniir/Legends|Ord Biniir]]. The victory was heavily [[Propaganda/Legends|propagandised]] by the Empire and Fel became an Imperial hero. Now considered an elite unit, the 181st was reduced in size to a group, and the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Group]] became one of the most glamorous Imperial units and attracted the Empire's finest pilots.<ref name="Empire'sService">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: In the Empire's Service]]''</ref>

By [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the TIE Interceptor formed twenty percent of the Starfighter Corps and was the craft of choice for elite units like the 181st Imperial Fighter Group. It was deployed in force alongside traditional TIE Fighters at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], but despite inflicting heavy losses upon the attacking [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]], was ultimately unable to prevent the destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]] and the death of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="Warfare" />

===After Endor===
[[File:Battle_of_Brentaal_by_Bruno_Werneck.jpg||left|thumb|The [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Group]] at the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]].]]
The [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] splintered among various rogue [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and [[Admiral/Legends|Admirals]] that set themselves up as [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] in the aftermath of Endor, with only a Loyalist rump remaining to defend [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage's]] ''de jure'' successor government on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Elite units like the 181st under [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] remained loyal, fighting against the advancing [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] at engagements like [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Brentaal IV]], but were ultimately unable to prevent the New Republic's [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation of Coruscant]] in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]].<ref name="Warfare" />

The collapse of centralized Imperial authority led to numerous changes in starfighter doctrine: Warlord [[Zsinj]] deployed the shielded, missile-equipped [[TIE/rpt starfighter|TIE Raptor]], a craft of his own design. Separated from the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] and traditional sources of recruitment, officers like [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] were forced to recognize that veteran [[TIE pilot]]s could no longer be treated as expendable assets. TIE Interceptors were retrofitted with [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], while poorly-armored TIE models were redesigned as support craft flown by [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]], resulting in the development of the [[TIE/D automated starfighter]].<ref name="Warfare" />

The Starfighter Corps and the rest of the Imperial Military was consolidated under a single command in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] after Admiral [[Natasi Daala]] and Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] [[Imperial Reunification|reunified the Empire]], forming the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. Starfighters were an integral element of the [[Orinda campaign]], the Remnant's first military offensive against the New Republic, and elite groups like the 181st, led by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Turr Phennir/Legends|Turr Phennir]], continued to [[Imperial Skirmishes|skirmish]] with the Republic until the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|Bastion Accords]] of [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]].<ref name="Warfare" />

Under the [[Fel Empire]] in [[130 ABY]], the Starfighter Corps remained skeptical of snubfighters and continued to prefer the ancient combination of [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptors]] and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]], with the heavily shielded [[Predator-class fighter|''Predator''-class fighter]] and the [[Neutralizer-class bomber|''Neutralizer''-class bomber]] filling its starfighter forces.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref>

==Organization==
===Administration===
The Starfighter Corps was under the purview of [[Flight Branch]], which was responsible for the flight operations of all the Empire's [[Warship/Legends|warships]], as well as all of the Empire's starfighters, including the pilots and support personnel.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

===Tactical organization===
The Starfighter Corps took most of its organization from the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]-era structure of the [[Republic Starfighter Corps/Legends|Republic Starfighter Corps]], though the positions of [[Fighter wing/Legends|fighter wings]] in the hierarchy were swapped:
*'''[[Flight/Legends|Element]]''': 2 starfighters, consisting of a leader and a [[Wingmate/Legends|wingmate]].
*'''[[Flight group/Legends|Flight]]''': 3 starfighters, or 4 starfighters in 2 elements.
*'''[[Squadron/Legends|Squadron]]''': 12 starfighters in 3 or 4 flights.
*'''[[Fighter wing/Legends|Wing]]''': 72 starfighters in 2 groups, typical complement of an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]

The typical formation of an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer's wing was four [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] squadrons (one squadron was often equipped to be a reconnaissance squadron with [[TIE/rc starfighter]]s), one squadron of [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bombers]] (lower priority ships had to make do with older [[TIE/gt starfighter|TIE/gt fighter-bombers]]), and one squadron of [[TIE/br boarding shuttle|TIE Boarding Craft]]. Often one or two flights in a fighter squadron were [[TIE/fc starfighter|TIE/FC fire control craft]]. Sometimes, well disciplined pilots flew in formations of five, including the leader who often operates in the center.<ref name="Rogue Leader Guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> Sometimes one of the fighter squadrons was used for training purposes. By the Battle of Endor, one squadron had been swapped out in favor of a squadron of TIE Interceptors.<ref name="Vehicles" /> During typical operations, two TIE squadrons provided screening for their Star Destroyer and any escort vessels, two conducted forward recon, and two were held in reserve.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> In addition, various units also placed authority on the leader, with the unit splitting apart if their leader was shot down.<ref name="Rogue Leader">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref><ref name="Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

TIE Fighters assigned to ground operations were Navy vessels, but their pilots reported to an [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] garrison commander, organized into [[ground support wing]]s.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The Navy's insistence on retaining control of all starfighters meant that ground support wings were smaller than those assigned to Star Destroyers, and consisted of forty TIEs in ten flights of four fighters each. Three flights were TIE Bombers, six were sorted into two [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] of TIE Fighters, and a single flight of [[TIE/fc starfighter|TIE/FC fire control craft]].<ref name="Sourcebook" /> Nonetheless, the ground support wings were considered a change from the pre-Clone Wars era Republic Military, where Army units generally were not allowed access to starfighters at all, in large part due to the Republic Navy having extremely strict control over its starfighters.<ref name="Sourcebook 2">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref>

==Personnel==
===Specializations===
The most visible members of the Starfighter Corps were the [[TIE pilot]]s. Distinguished by all-[[black]] [[Flight suit/Legends|flight suits]] and bulky, fully-enclosed, vacuum-sealed helmets, the Empire at its height produced millions of TIE pilots, and generally considered them expendable assets. The TIE pilots formed the elite of the [[Flight Branch]],<ref name="Handbook" /> and in fact regarded the lack of protection in TIE Fighters to be a testament to this, and to their abilities. Serving TIE pilots rarely supported the intermittent attempts by [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] to champion the introduction of better-protected starfighters. The rivalry between ground- and space-based pilots was legendary, which could often lead to drunken [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] brawls between "ground-hogs" and "vac-heads".<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Other specializations included ground crew, providing maintenance and technical support for squadrons.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The [[Imperial gunner/Legends|Imperial gunners]] were a special sub-unit of the Corps.<ref name="Owner's Technical Manual" /> Even though they did not make it to becoming [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], Imperial gunners nonetheless possessed keen eyes, superior reflexes, and a rapport with specialized equipment, and as such they were tasked to use their skills with weapons to handle the powerful [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]] and [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]] of Imperial [[Starship/Legends|vessels]], such as [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and [[World Devastator]]s. They were trained on handling light, medium and heavy turbolasers, as well as ion cannons, missile launchers and tractor beams.<ref name="Handbook" /> The [[Cruisemissile trooper]]s were a specialized variant of the TIE pilots that were specifically trained to operate the [[Cruisemissile assault craft]]s, acting as the spearheads for the Imperial Navy, and by extension, the Starfighter Corps. Unlike standard TIE pilots and the fighters they were assigned to, however, the cruisemissile troopers were affixed to their craft from the waist down.<ref name="PotF2">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|pack=Cruisemissile Trooper|link=potf2cruisemissile.asp}}, description on the back of the toy box</ref>

===Training===
[[File:Flight_School.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Flight school cadets learning advanced techniques.]]
Starfighter Corps training occurred after basic training at the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]]. Flight training was reserved for the top five percent of graduates of the [[Sector Naval Academy|Sector Naval Academies]], and the top third of graduates from the [[Imperial Naval Academy/Legends|Imperial Naval Academy]] on [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt IV]].<ref name="Sourcebook" /> The Empire operated various [[Flight school/Legends|flight schools]] on capital ships, [[Planet/Legends|planets]] or [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] bases. The most prestigious was the [[Vensenor Flight Academy/Legends|Flight Academy]] housed aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Vensenor/Legends|''Vensenor'']].<ref name="Warfare" />

At flight school, a trainee pilot would be assigned to a partner and learn to operate as a team in combat through hundreds of hours of flight drills. Attrition was high: at one point flight training had a ninety percent failure rate. Fatalities in training were common, especially after [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]] were assigned to actual combat missions.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

In some cases, they also trained their pilots via simulations of past battles, with there being at least four training operations for each vehicle. Completing a certain number of training missions had them being presented with a special medallion signifying their completion of the required training, with three for each vehicle. The Bronze medallion was awarded to those who completed half of the necessary training requirements. Silver was likewise awarded to those who completed three quarters of the necessary training requirements. Gold, lastly was awarded to those who completed all the necessary training. Similarly, [[training patch]]es for various Imperial craft were also issued to any pilots who did at least five laps in the training simulator.<ref name="TIE Fighter">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

===Ranks===
[[Flight Branch]] [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank insignia plaques]] were similar to those of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. The branch's specialist ranks included [[General/Legends|General]], [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]], [[Major/Legends|Major]], [[Commander/Legends|Commander]], [[Flight Captain]], [[Flight Lieutenant]], and [[Flight officer/Legends|Flight Officer]], which were the equivalent of [[Rear Admiral/Legends|Rear Admiral]], [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]], [[Senior Commander/Legends|Senior Commander]], [[Junior Commander/Legends|Junior Commander]], [[Senior Lieutenant/Legends|Senior Lieutenant]], [[Junior Lieutenant/Legends|Junior Lieutenant]], and [[Ensign/Legends|Ensign]], respectively, in the Navy's [[Line Branch]].<ref name="Warfare" />

For the junior ranks of Captain and lower, their titles were prefixed by "Flight". TIE pilots in command positions also used positional titles, including [[Squadron Leader/Legends|Squadron Leader]], [[Group Captain]] and [[Wing Commander/Legends|Wing Commander]]. The very few pilots promoted beyond General were promoted into the Line Branch at the rank of [[Vice Admiral/Legends|Vice Admiral]], although they generally retained the honorific branch title of [[Air Marshal]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Another honorable rank given to very few pilots was the rank of [[Baron of the Empire|Flight Baron]]. Pilots who had this title wore red streaks on their black pilot uniforms. One notable figure who held this rank is [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]].

==Equipment==
===Uniforms===
Outside of combat, the Starfighter Corps wore the same olive-grey [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|military uniforms]] as the rest of the Imperial Navy. In some cases, veterans like [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Yorr/Legends|Yorr]],<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]],<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> and [[Ace/Legends|ace]] [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone pilots]] were honored with all-black dress uniforms similar to those of the non-commissioned officers of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]].<ref name="ROTSICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> Pilots in action wore all-[[black]] [[Flight suit/Legends|flight suits]] and fully-enclosed, vacuum-sealed helmets displaying the [[Imperial crest/Legends|Imperial crest]].<ref name="Visual Guide">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The helmets themselves bore a strong enough resemblance to [[Stormtrooper armor|Stormtrooper helmets]] that the official field manual for the Empire's military forces, ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', had to specifically state that the pilots, despite the appearance of the helmets, belonged strictly to the Imperial Navy, and were not [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtroopers]].<ref name="Handbook" />

Elite units were permitted to customize their uniforms and craft: the aces of the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing/Legends|181st Imperial Fighter Group]] wore red piping along the arms and legs of their flight suits and uniforms, as well as the wings of their TIE Interceptors, signifying that they had achieved ten kills in combat.<ref name="Empire'sService" />

Owing to their being a specialized version of the TIE pilots, the cruisemissile troopers wore similar uniforms to the ones used by TIE pilots while in action, although the primary difference is that the colors of the uniforms are inverted (i.e., the main color is white, and the Imperial crests on their helmets are black).<ref name="PotF2" />

===Weapons===
Some TIE pilots carried [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] as sidearms in the event that they were shot down.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> However, since the odds of a pilot surviving a crash were low, standard issue of personal weapons was rare.

Ceremonial [[Parade saber|sabers]] were issued as part of the Corps' dress uniform: officers who had been dishonorably discharged would have their [[Sword/Legends|swords]] broken as a sign of their disgrace.<ref name="Warfare" /> [[File:Imperial_Fleet.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Imperial fleet]]

===Vehicles===
{{Main|TIE series/Legends}}
The primary craft of the Starfighter Corps were the immense number of variants of the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]]. By far the most common were the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]], the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]], and the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]]. Less common were the older [[TIE/gt starfighter|TIE/gt fighter-bomber]], the [[TIE/fc starfighter|TIE/fc fire control craft]], and the [[TIE/rc starfighter|TIE/rc reconnaissance starfighter]].

As the Galactic Civil War ground on, the Starfighter Corps developed a series of experimental TIE variants designed to combat Rebel snubfighters, including the shielded, [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]-capable and [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedo]]-equipped [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]], the [[TIE/hu "Hunter" Multi-Role Starfighter|TIE Hunter]], and the [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter/Legends|TIE/ph phantom]], an exceedingly rare variant developed by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]], equipped with a [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]].

Although their most well known starfighter ordnance was the TIE series, they also had access to other types of fighters as well. A notable example of starfighters outside the TIE series was the [[Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wing/Legends|''Alpha''-class Xg-1 Star Wing]] and the [[Missile Boat]]. However, the latter ultimately was shelved until further notice, both due to a near-theft of [[Sealion|one of the prototypes]] and [[Destruction of the Missile Boat facilities|events]] caused by a coup from [[Demetrius Zaarin|one]] of the [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]].<ref name="TIE Fighter" /><ref name="TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM guide">''[[TIE Fighter Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref>
